# workflows

CI and release workflows.

| Workflow | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`pages.yml`](pages.yml) | Builds the project site: the pages in [`site/`](../../site/README.md) in both languages, the introduction, the language tour and the page of the tools, which links to the files of the desktop viewer's newest tag `viewer-vX.Y.Z`; the pages of the language standard with [`scripts/spec/`](../../scripts/spec/README.md); the RNL skill package, its zip and plain-text files and `llms.txt` with [`scripts/skill/`](../../scripts/skill/build.py), the entry for agents; and the web viewer of [`apps/web`](../../apps/web/README.md) with its samples, at `viewer/`, for which it installs Rust with the WebAssembly target, Node and Python, and writes the web fonts with [`scripts/fonts.py`](../../scripts/README.md). It keeps the Cargo registry and the core's WebAssembly build between runs, and the web fonts until `scripts/fonts.py` changes. On pull requests that touch the site, the standard or what the web viewer is built from, it only checks the build, which fails when a text lacks one of its languages, a check of the standard fails or the web viewer does not build; on `main` it also publishes the site to GitHub Pages. It runs on `main` again after `spec-release.yml` succeeds, so that the pages of the standard carry the new revision label, and after `viewer-release.yml` ("Viewer release") succeeds, so that the page of the tools links to the new release; only `main` may deploy to the `github-pages` environment, and only the deploy job may write to Pages. Pages must use "GitHub Actions" as its source. |
| [`skill.yml`](skill.yml) | Checks the RNL skill package in [`skills/`](../../skills/README.md): builds the `rnl` command, requires that the files generated from the package files are what they give, that the package is whole, and that every netlist in it reads with `rnl check` without errors or warnings ([`scripts/skill`](../../scripts/skill/build.py)). Runs on pushes to `main` and on pull requests that touch the package, its script, the short guide, the pages for agents, the standard library or the crates. |
| [`spec-release.yml`](spec-release.yml) | On a tag such as `spec-0.2-r1`, builds every form of that version of the standard and attaches them to the GitHub release "RNL 0.2, revision 1"; the tag's message becomes the release notes ([decision 0007](../../docs/decisions/0007-publishing-the-standard.md)). |
| [`desktop.yml`](desktop.yml) | Checks formatting, runs clippy and the tests of the desktop viewer in [`apps/desktop`](../../apps/desktop/README.md) on Linux, Windows and macOS, with the web fonts of the page it embeds written by [`scripts/fonts.py`](../../scripts/README.md), and checks every script of the page, [`apps/viewer-ui`](../../apps/viewer-ui/README.md), and of the app's tests. On Windows it also runs the app's smoke test, which drives it through WebView2's DevTools port. Runs on pushes to `main` and on pull requests that touch the viewer, its page, the crates, the standard library, the font script or the netlist the smoke test opens. |
| [`viewer-release.yml`](viewer-release.yml) | Builds the desktop viewer for Windows on GitHub's Windows runner, with Rust's MSVC toolchain, the web fonts and the Tauri command line that [`apps/desktop/package.json`](../../apps/desktop/package.json) pins: the app as a single executable, an NSIS installer for the current user and an MSI for the machine ([Building](../../apps/desktop/README.md#building)), with their SHA-256 sums. It requires that a tag names the app's version and that the release has notes, checks with `dumpbin` that the executable imports no `WebView2Loader.dll`, smoke-tests the executable alone in a directory, and installs each installer silently, smoke-tests the installed app and uninstalls it. Runs on a pushed tag `viewer-v<version>`, and then publishes the GitHub release titled `RNL Viewer <version>` with the notes of `apps/desktop/release-notes/<version>.md` and the four files, not marked as the repository's latest release, which stays the language standard's; run by hand, it only builds and keeps the files as the run's artifact ([Releasing](../../apps/desktop/README.md#releasing)). |
| [`publish-runtime.yml`](publish-runtime.yml) | On a tag such as `runtime-v0.1.0-preview.7`, builds the runtime package of [`bindings/runtime-wasm`](../../bindings/runtime-wasm/README.md) at the tag's version, tests its modules, checks what npm gets and publishes it to npm as `@rich-netlist/runtime` under the dist-tag `next`, with provenance; only versions with a pre-release suffix for now. The build runs in a job that cannot publish; the publishing job publishes by trusted publishing, with the OIDC permission and no token. The package is smoke-tested in a minimal frontend built with Vite ([`packages/runtime/smoke`](../../packages/runtime/smoke/README.md)) in Chromium: the tarball before a publish, the version from npm after. On a pull request that changes the package, and when run by hand with `dry_run`, it builds and checks it only. |
| [`viewer.yml`](viewer.yml) | Tests the viewers' shared page in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit with Playwright, against a fake shell, and smoke-tests the web viewer's site with the core as WebAssembly ([`tests/viewer`](../../tests/viewer/README.md)), on Linux; installs Rust with the WebAssembly target and the browsers with what they need, and keeps the report of a failed run. Runs on pushes to `main` and on pull requests that touch the page, the web viewer, the bindings, the tests, the conformance corpus, the crates or the standard library. |
| [`rust.yml`](rust.yml) | Checks formatting, runs clippy and the tests of the Rust workspace on Linux, Windows and macOS. On Linux it also builds the core crates and the WebAssembly binding in [`bindings/runtime-wasm`](../../bindings/runtime-wasm/README.md), tests the binding's JavaScript modules, and requires that native and WebAssembly builds give identical Documents on the conformance corpus and the standard packages; and it downloads the pinned fonts and requires that the renderer's font metrics are what they give (`python scripts/fonts.py metrics --check`). Runs on pushes to `main` and on pull requests that touch the crates, the bindings, the standard library, the test corpora or the font script; changes to the page's tests in `tests/viewer` alone are left to `viewer.yml`. |
| [`web.yml`](web.yml) | Builds the web viewer in [`apps/web`](../../apps/web/README.md) on Linux: the web fonts with [`scripts/fonts.py`](../../scripts/README.md), the core as WebAssembly and the site with the samples; checks every script of the site with `node --check`, and that the site is served with the MIME types a browser needs. Runs on pushes to `main` and on pull requests that touch the web viewer, the page, the bindings, the crates, the standard library, the font script or the conformance corpus, which gives the samples. |

`pages.yml` and `spec-release.yml` install pandoc, Typst and the CJK fonts at pinned versions through the local action [`install-spec-tools`](../actions/install-spec-tools/action.yml), which checks the SHA-256 of each download against the one its GitHub release gives.

Every action is pinned to the commit of its release, with the release in a comment after it, such as `actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1`, so that a tag moved later cannot change what runs. To update one, pin the commit its new release's tag names. `publish-runtime.yml` installs npm by an exact version too.

See the [roadmap](../../docs/roadmap.md) for planned work.
